title: HPC Workload Manager ↔ Remote Quantum Resource Boundary
boundary_mechanism: QRMI-class interface + WLM plugins/hooks + optional second-level middleware scheduler

unknowns.question: What does acquire establish across implementations?
If WLM-visible availability and provider state disagree, which controls dispatch?
Who has final authority when calibration or maintenance conflicts with an allocation?
What proves that a remote task stopped after scheduler cancellation or timeout?
What is the recovery authority after partial failure?
Can one record reconcile allocated time, provider waiting, actual execution, retry/cancellation and cost?
How are HPC identity and provider credential authority joined and audited?

known: Remote QPU integration can introduce a second queue outside classical scheduler direct control
acquire is not synonymous with execution readiness in the general case
Calibration can invalidate WLM availability assumptions after allocation
Credential and accounting mechanisms exist in multiple distinct models; the current evidence pack does not establish a single interoperable authority or audit model
assumed: No unpublished site-private production contract is treated as public evidence
Local WLM job end is not assumed to equal remote termination without provider-side evidence
evidence_boundary: Public QRMI/OpenQSE/HPC-QC materials end before full cross-domain precedence, termination proof, recovery matrix, and reconciled accounting contracts

gate.second_proving_domain: advanced multi-die/chiplet with distributed control or management authority
